formats.key: mint(address collateralToken, uint256 collateralAmount, uint256 txDeadline, uint256 minFtUSDOut)
effects: The contract takes exactly collateralAmount of collateralToken from the signer (safeTransferFrom in _executeMintWithRelayerFee) and deposits it in the yield wrapper.

ftUSD is minted at the oracle price, capped by the per-collateral hardcap. The mint fee is kept by the contract, and the net amount goes to the signer (msg.sender). The call reverts if the net amount is below minFtUSDOut.
When payoutRouter is set, the net ftUSD goes through the rate-limited router, router.payout(recipient,...). The router may pay the signer later instead of in this transaction.
The call reverts after txDeadline. A txDeadline of 0 means no deadline.
formats.shown: Buy ftUSD: pay {collateralAmount} {collateralToken}, receive at least {minFtUSDOut} ftUSD, with a deadline date. The interpolated intent is 'Buy {minFtUSDOut}'.

findings.title: mint interpolatedIntent 'Buy {minFtUSDOut}' states the minimum as the amount bought and omits the payment.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json mint interpolatedIntent "Buy {minFtUSDOut}". Case 0 renders "Buy 4.968328 ftUSD", but the signer received 4.993295 ftUSD and paid 4.994694 USDC, which the sentence does not mention.

findings.title: mint: the rate-limited payout router can delay ftUSD delivery, and nothing on screen says so.
findings.evidence: MintAndRedeem.sol _executeMintWithRelayerFee: `if (address(router) != address(0)) { ...safeTransfer(address(router), netFtUSDAmount); router.payout(recipient, netToRecipient, executor, relayerFeeFtUSDAmount); }`. The MintQueued event exists. In case 0 the ftUSD went through router 0xf69d82e2… before reaching the signer.
findings.fix: Rename the 'Minimum receive' label, or add a note, to say that ftUSD may be queued when rate limits apply.

findings.title: mint deadline: a txDeadline of 0 means 'no deadline' but would render as a 1970 date.
findings.evidence: MintAndRedeem.sol _enforceDeadline: `if (txDeadline == 0) return;`. descriptor.json field txDeadline uses format date with no special case for 0.
findings.fix: Show 'No deadline' when txDeadline is 0, if the spec allows it, or explain it in the label.

cases.notes: The signer paid 4.994694 USDC, shown exactly as Pay. The signer received 4.993295 ftUSD, which is at least the shown minimum of 4.968328 ftUSD. The mint fee was 0 here. The ftUSD passed through the payout router 0xf69d… before reaching the signer.

formats.key: redeem(address collateralToken, uint256 ftUSDAmount, uint256 txDeadline, uint256 minCollateralOut)
effects: The contract takes exactly ftUSDAmount ftUSD from the signer (safeTransferFrom in _executeRedeemWithRelayerFee). The redeem fee in ftUSD is kept by the contract, and the rest is burned.
The collateral amount is computed from the oracle price, capped by the average-mint and NAV rates, and must be at least minCollateralOut.

The collateral is released by yieldWrapper.withdraw(collateralToRecipient, signer). The wrapper is rate-limited and returns a queueId, so the collateral may be queued and not delivered to the signer in this transaction.
The call reverts after txDeadline. A txDeadline of 0 means no deadline.
formats.shown: Sell ftUSD: pay {ftUSDAmount} ftUSD, receive at least {minCollateralOut} {collateralToken}, with a deadline date. The interpolated intent is 'Sell {ftUSDAmount}'.

findings.title: redeem says 'Minimum receive' collateral, but the collateral went to a queue address, not to the signer.
findings.evidence: Case 1 mined: the signer's only effect is −8438969 ftUSD. The 8440233 USDC left wrapper 0x8eaf42f3… for 0x5f19315b…, not the signer 0x07f963bb…. MintAndRedeem.sol _executeRedeemWithRelayerFee: `queueIdTo = wrapper.withdraw(collateralToRecipient, p.recipient);` with the comment 'it handles rate limiting of collateral outflows'. redeem returns (collateralAmount, queueId). The descriptor's minCollateralOut field is labelled 'Minimum receive', which implies the signer gets the collateral now.
findings.fix: Change the label and intent to say the collateral may be queued for a later claim, for example 'Minimum collateral (may be queued)' and 'Sell {ftUSDAmount} for at least {minCollateralOut}, possibly queued'.

findings.title: redeem interpolatedIntent 'Sell {ftUSDAmount}' omits the collateral asset and its minimum.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json redeem interpolatedIntent "Sell {ftUSDAmount}". Case 1 renders "Sell 8.438969 ftUSD", with no USDC in the sentence.

findings.title: redeem deadline: a txDeadline of 0 means 'no deadline' but would render as a 1970 date.
findings.evidence: MintAndRedeem.sol _enforceDeadline: `if (txDeadline == 0) return;`. The descriptor's txDeadline field is a plain date.
findings.fix: Show 'No deadline' when txDeadline is 0, or explain it in the label.

cases.notes: The ftUSD out (8.438969) was shown and understood correctly. The reader also expected at least 8.398031 USDC to arrive, but none reached the signer in this transaction: 8.440233 USDC went from the wrapper to 0x5f19…, which looks like a rate-limit queue. The screen led the reader to expect funds this call did not deliver.

couldNotCheck: The yield wrapper 0x8eaf42f3c8c06f4dcf2270d83eb5f443e3fa9ce9 (IftYieldWrapperV2.withdraw) is not in the directory. It decides whether redeem collateral reaches the signer now or is queued (case 1 sent it to 0x5f19315ba3b54f3641c10d21006ef95f7b5f2cc6).
The payout router 0xf69d82e2f647f92821c2d2520726c4ee7660ece5 (IMintPayoutRouter.payout) is not in the directory. It decides when and how much minted ftUSD the signer receives.
The ftUSD core 0xf02f09f82b1d725d823ee2deac1995dcef8e0787 (core.mint/core.burn) is not in the directory.
